author: jackclarkSF
text: @scottlegrand I'm interested in analogies - different political parties have different views on science with regard to weather and climate change, but the civil weather forecasting and analysis infrastructure has done a reasonable job equipping us with decent information and projections.

author: jackclarkSF
text: @scottlegrand If we had a political party in power that was super excited about technology, then things would move in a positive direction. But even without that, there are 1000s of non-political appointees in government tasked with making sense of technology and they're not being used well

author: jackclarkSF
text: @scottlegrand It's useful to disentangle different policy infrastructures here: the politicized stuff is less easy to work with (so I agree with spirit of your question). But lots of these agencies are civil/bipartisan in nature - and they're not being as effective as they could be.

author: jackclarkSF
text: @_sunilrawat Interesting! Go on? One thing I'm a fan of is creation of a ton of DARPA-style competitions in different areas. We don't know exactly what to do, but competitions feel like a cheap way to generate powerful signals about things to subsequently invest in.
